what_happened: Compiled probe (specs/evidence/cone-unravelling-frame-layer-split/cone-core-probe.lean) validated the full structural core of the cone unravelling in one pass: IsOrientedForest (coneRin E), double seriality of coneR on the LITERAL sum carrier W + (W x List W) with no coherence subtype, the projection homomorphism, and the four transport identities the two-layer Saturation split rests on.

Reynolds' Auxiliary Atoms rule has no statement in the corpus: literature-search.sh returns nothing for 'auxiliary atoms' in a formal-logic sense, and reynolds_2001's sub-index skips the axiom-system sections 5-8 where the rule would sit (TOC jumps 4.7-4.8 -> 9). Research proceeded with NamingRules.lean's recorded Saturation obligation as the source of record, which is the task's actual target.

Compile-checked the plan's seven pinned Lean Challenge Statements via lean-challenge-snapshot.sh --dry-run --compile before writing them as the plan's contract; the assembled module reported 'compile: OK', so every pinned signature is known well-formed at plan time rather than discovered wrong at implement time.

The challenge-snapshot extractor chunks at the declaration keyword and strips a per-declaration 'open X in' prefix, so the headline theorem's 'open FormalSystem.PlusLanguage in' form (which UniversalCover.lean uses) left the extracted module unable to resolve PlusFormula/PlusTruthAt. Resolved by opening PlusLanguage at the top of the Challenge block and recording in the plan that the real module keeps the 'open ... in' form.

validate-artifact.sh flagged a Phase 3 'Files to modify' entry whose free-text annotation contained backticked LEMMA names, which the harvester reads as a second path on the same line. Resolved by removing the backticked names from the annotation and pointing at the phase's task list instead.

Phases 1-2 of the plan are a promotion of an already-compiled 295-line probe (specs/evidence/cone-unravelling-frame-layer-split/cone-core-probe.lean) with zero errors at the pinned toolchain; no proof re-derivation was needed for the structural core.

Phase 3's task list names 'via coneRin_bwd_subsingleton and seg_subsingleton' as the route for subsingleton_of_subset_range_inr. seg_subsingleton is inapplicable: it demands IsOrientedForest (coneR E), which is false (the inl layer is a verbatim copy of E and inherits its loops/opposite edges). The lemma was proved at its named statement via coneRin_bwd_unique alone (through iter_inr_fwd); the inapplicability is recorded in the lemma's own doc comment.

Phase 5 BLOCKED: every frame-assembly signature the plan declares (coneFrameOfSerial, coneF_twoWayBounded_of_constraints, and the pinned Challenge statement exists_coneUnravelling_of_constraints) omits a base-Saturation hypothesis the cone construction provably requires. Machine-checked refutations of the three escape routes: a bare FrameOver carries no axiom (TaskFrame.lean:1072); C+S+L does not imply Saturation (constraints_pairwise_independent's rayRel conjunct); IsOrientedForest (coneR E) is false since the inl layer copies E. Necessity is exhibited by the family {Fib (ofStepRel (coneR E)) (.inl w) 1 | w : Z} at E := (w <= u) on Z. The pinned headline is satisfiable only by delegating to the universal cover's existing theorem, which would assert nothing about this module. Escalated rather than adding the hypothesis, per rules/plan-compliance.md Statement Fidelity.

git-commit-scoped.sh's V10 file_scope-containment guard dropped three paths that are genuinely this task's deliverables: FormalSystem/Semantics/README.md (the hand-maintained inventory row check-module-invariants.sh demands for a new module), scripts/nolint-attribute-allowlist.txt (the C26-required paired entry), and specs/evidence/cone-unravelling-frame-layer-split/cone-core-probe.lean (named in the plan's Phase 6 task list). The task's declared file_scope, set at creation, anticipated none of them. Resolved by a second commit without --task, which is the guard's documented opt-in boundary; both diffs were verified to contain only this dispatch's own lines first.

FormalSystem/Semantics/ConeUnravelling.lean landed: 842 lines, 34 declarations, sorry-free, axiom-clean, full library build green with zero warnings. Phases 1-4 complete and committed, with saturation_coneR -- the two-layer Saturation split -- proved at its pinned signature; 6 of 7 pinned Challenge statements are proved as pinned. Phase 5 is BLOCKED: every frame-assembly signature the plan declares, including the pinned exists_coneUnravelling_of_constraints, omits a base-Saturation hypothesis the cone construction provably requires, and all three escape routes are machine-checked closed. A one-line user decision between two named corrected signatures unblocks the remaining Phase 5 and all of Phase 6.

Plan revision found three live constraint-form citations in ConeUnravelling.lean (lines 23, 114, 792), not the one the first pass assumed; grepping the module instead of trusting the recorded line range turned a partial docstring fix into a complete one before it reached the implementer.

The recorded Challenge statements had already been amended to the instance-projected form by an earlier cycle (plan mtime 15:55Z, first decision 15:41Z), so this forced --plan round found the headline signature correct but its Phase 5 routing still pointing at the _of_constraints API (taskRel_eq_iter_of_constraints, plus_invariance_of_isZTime_of_constraints) that option (b) drops; the amendment had no fidelity-trail note either. Phase 5's bridge lemma, coneFrame/taskRel/isRegular trio and coneF_twoWayBounded all landed essentially first-try against the UniversalCover.lean template; the only failure was omega being unable to see Int linear-arithmetic facts about x : up-intOrder when deriving x.natAbs = n + 1, replaced by Nat.exists_eq_succ_of_ne_zero + Int.natAbs_ne_zero.

check-module-invariants C34a rejected 'Constraints consumed: Compositionality, Seriality, Limit' on base_taskRel_eq_ofStepRel and coneF_twoWayBounded because their [F.IsRegular] binder also supplies Saturation. UniversalCover.lean's instance-projected declarations are excused by binder-free twins; this module has none by the recorded user decision, so the markers were corrected to list all four constraints with the reason stated inline.

Three prose occurrences of literal tokens ('_of_constraints', 'sorry') inside the new doc comments tripped Phase 5's and Phase 6's own literal grep criteria, even though no declaration used either. Each was rephrased without substance change. A plan whose verification criteria are bare greps over a module makes its own explanatory prose a tripwire.

All five measured axiom profiles in the new evidence module compiled green on the first #guard_msgs run, because they were read off lean_verify rather than typed from the OrientedForestSaturationTest template; coneF_surjective's axiom-free profile would have been wrong if copied.
